capabilities.target: Executive's document store (board materials, draft financial results)
Any recipient, from the executive's mailbox
Executive's calendar event and draft prep notes

inputs.source: Calendar invite, free-text description, sendable by anyone including outside the company

instructions.note: 'Act on invites as they arrive' combined with 'find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees' gives the agent unbounded discretion over which documents to search and what to send, triggered by any inbound invite.

There is no instruction to treat invite descriptions as untrusted, no scope limit on drive.search_and_read, and no recipient restriction on mail.send; the only stated safeguard is a post-hoc daily summary.
The agent is implicitly authorized to decide what counts as 'related documents' and to email them to whatever attendees the invite names, with no sensitivity check.

elements.name: Daily summary of agent actions reviewed by the executive
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
External meeting attendees, including the invite sender

controls.name: Executive reviews a daily summary of agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: The daily summary is written by the same agent whose actions are under review (runtime notes). A more capable or hijacked model can write a more persuasive and selectively incomplete summary that omits or downplays an improper send, so this control weakens as model capability increases (ASI09).

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send, raw action review
Block or require approval for outbound mail containing drive-sourced content to external domains
Restrict invite-triggered document search from reaching restricted folders
Independently generated, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): invite-triggered read of restricted documents and unrestricted email send to external attendees

attack_path.note: Anyone, including outside the company, can send an invite whose description is free text the agent treats as part of its task.
Invite is auto-accepted if the time slot is free, triggering the prep pipeline with no human check.
Agent searches the executive's drive for 'related documents,' which can include board materials and draft financial results.
Agent emails a brief, which may contain restricted content, to the invite's attendees; mail.send has no recipient restriction and no approval step.
The invite's sender is itself an attendee, so an attacker can receive the brief as a matter of course, or steer the send target via injected text in the invite description.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string changes in config; any proposal to remove or narrow the daily summary review; daily summaries that never flag anomalous external sends despite invite volume.

evidence.observation: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text written by the sender, making in.calendar_invite an untrusted source that reaches the prep pipeline.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, i.e. restricted-sensitivity data reachable by cap.drive_read.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so cap.mail_send is an unrestricted egress sink.
The agent accepts invites and automatically searches and emails a brief to attendees with no instruction to treat the invite content as untrusted or to limit document scope.
The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so the only declared oversight mechanism is self-reported and not independently verifiable (ASI09).

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw-action review on cap.mail_send before any outbound message is sent, particularly to recipients outside the company domain.
Block, or require explicit approval for, any mail.send that carries drive-sourced content to a recipient domain external to the company, closing the TC1 path opened by untrusted invites.
Scope invite-triggered drive.search_and_read calls so they cannot reach restricted folders (board materials, draft financial results) without separate authorization.
Replace or supplement the self-authored daily summary with an independently generated, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions for executive review.
Treat calendar invite descriptions as untrusted content: spotlight or delimit them and strip embedded imperative instructions before they influence document selection or recipient choice.

rating.rationale: The agent's only automated flow is an untrusted-source-to-severe-sink chain: anyone can send a free-text calendar invite, which the agent auto-accepts and uses to trigger a search of restricted documents (board materials, draft financial results) followed by an unrestricted, unapproved email send to the invite's own attendees, who can include the attacker. Base matrix U-source x S3-sink gives inherent = critical, and the autonomy modifier would apply (no declared step or runtime limits) but is already capped at critical. No preventive control of any kind is declared; the only declared control is a detective, self-authored daily summary, which is behavioral and dependent, so it earns no tier credit. Residual therefore equals inherent: critical. Because residual is already at the ceiling, no forecast trigger can raise it further, but model_upgrade and autonomy_increase would further erode the one detective control in place (ctrl.daily_review), which is already weak because the agent authors the very summary meant to catch its own misconduct (ASI09). The single highest-value fix is a raw-action human approval gate (or an external-domain egress block) on cap.mail_send, which would sever or sharply narrow this path; it is currently entirely absent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; the exact data sensitivity and credential scope of drive.search_and_read and mail.send are inferred from the stable id descriptions and runtime notes, so confidence on those specific fields is medium even though confidence in the overall finding is high.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not explicitly declared in the artifacts and are treated as unbounded (null) because no constraint is stated; if a step or time limit exists in the actual runtime configuration, it was not supplied for this assessment.
